page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 20 vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation. System memory consists of 256.0 GB of RAM, providing 12.8 GB per core. The primary hardware accelerator setup comprises three NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined 144 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 4190.38 and a Geekbench single-core score of 3088.0, both placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 84070.24 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17663.0, placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is also strong, reaching 3984.93 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 306.94 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 38.86 GB/sec and a Passmark CPU encryption score of 35487.74.

The shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, non-burstable CPU performance, though the underlying AMD EPYC 9575F hardware mitigates this with high baseline single-core execution speeds. The lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage configurations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU VRAM (144 GB) relative to the 20 vCPUs offers a resource-dense profile for memory-heavy parallel computing without paying for excessive CPU cores. This server is configured for GPU-accelerated workloads, machine learning model training, large-scale rendering, and data science jobs.
